startup.name: Percival
startup.description: AI copilot that helps researchers analyze and transform real world data, working on messy datasets from cleaning to analysis. Three person team in San Francisco and remote, Spring 2025 batch, tags Developer Tools, Data Science and AI. The buyer is unclear: academic labs, biotech or corporate research groups, paying for seats or usage.

yc_acceptance.basis: Starting prior is about 1 percent for a random applicant (0.6 to 2 percent, references/yc_acceptance.md). Up slightly for a technical, AI native pitch in a clear pain point, since researchers spend large time cleaning data. Down because the input shows no traction, the team has three people, the buyer is unclear and general chat assistants already analyse data. Net about 2 percent; the company is already in the batch so this is for completeness.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most likely say that AI data analysis is a crowded space where general assistants and Julius already let people upload data and ask questions, and that researchers, especially academics, have little budget. Partners would ask for a named paying segment and why a copilot would beat a general model for this job.

anchors.adjustment_reason: Window is 19.4 months, from 2025-04-07 to 2026-11-17, and counts a round above about 1M from outside investors closing inside it. Anchor 0.55 for Developer Tools and 0.59 for B2B, ever. A 19 month window covers the 2022 and later p75 time to seed (14 to 20 months), so about 80 percent of eventual seeds fit: 0.55 times 0.8 gives 0.44, then 0.38 for a three person team and an unclear buyer. 0.38 is 0.7x of the tag anchor. Hot AI interest is not lifted above the anchor, per the winners test. These odds do not rank this company against others.

bands.rationale: Small post YC round under 3M, common for three person developer tools teams with early users.
Institutional seed near the 2022 and later median of 3.5M to 4.1M if paying users grow.
Strong seed if a biotech or pharma customer base pays quickly; the 6M to 10M quartile applies to AI native companies with larger teams.
Large seed in AI for science, where a few companies raised big early rounds; rare for three people.

ladder.why_it_fails: The seed step fails if paying users stay as academics and students on small plans, because investors need a segment with budget such as pharma or industry research. MantleBio (scientific data tooling) raised a seed and then shut down, Deepnote needed years and a notebook niche to reach a Series A, and Julius competes for the same general analysts. A three person team also has limited capacity to sell into enterprises.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Tools for data analysis are being absorbed by general assistants, so most such companies stall, are acquired by a data platform for the team, or shut down like MantleBio. A large outcome needs a specific research workflow with budget and data that general tools cannot reach.

killers.risk: General AI assistants (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini) analyze uploaded data well enough, so a copilot has no edge
killers.evidence: OpenAI shipped data analysis in ChatGPT in 2023 and model providers keep adding code and chart features at no extra price.
killers.mitigation: Win on reproducible, auditable pipelines and domain data connectors that general tools lack.

killers.risk: Researchers have small budgets and long procurement, so revenue per seat stays low
killers.evidence: Academic labs fund tools through grants and per seat prices for similar tools sit near 20 to 100 dollars a month.
killers.mitigation: Sell to pharma, biotech or corporate R and D where budgets are larger.

killers.risk: Three person team cannot cover product, data integrations and sales at once
killers.evidence: The input lists three people, while research data comes in many formats that need constant integration work.
killers.mitigation: Focus on one data type or discipline and hire after revenue.

technical_complexity.rationale: Running code, cleaning data and charting with a model is standard, and a small team can build a first copilot in three months. The hard part is reliability on messy real data, reproducibility that researchers can cite, and connectors to domain formats.

takeover_risk.rationale: General assistants already offer file upload and code execution, and each model release improves them. A well resourced rival can add research workflows within months, so absorption risk is very high.

evidence.claim: Researchers spend a large share of analysis time on cleaning and formatting data, which is the pain this product targets (opinion pieces cite about 80 percent)
Many AI data analysis assistants already sell to the same users, which shows demand and price pressure

pros.evidence: Commentary and vendor blogs report most analysis time goes to data preparation.

narrative.headline: An AI data copilot for researchers facing general assistants; a seed in 19 months is possible but a Series A inside the window is unlikely.
narrative.general_summary: Percival offers an AI copilot for analysing research data from a three person team. Cohort anchors give 55 to 59 percent seed ever and about 80 percent of those land inside 19 months, so the estimate is 38 percent after a discount for team size and an unclear buyer. The main risk is absorption by general assistants and a weak paying segment. Direct YC analogs such as Julius, Deepnote and MantleBio show both the demand and the narrow paying segment. Later rounds inside the window are tail events. The odds do not rank this company against others.

assumptions: The input has no traction data; seed odds assume a normal Spring 2025 developer tools company.
Window 19.4 months; seed means a round above about 1M from outside investors closing inside it.
